questions.question: Select the correct synonym of 'Fortify'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. Strengthen**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'Fortify'** means to strengthen, secure, or reinforce something. (मजबूत करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The soldiers worked hard to fortify the walls of the castle to protect it from enemies.
 
 
• **'Strengthen'** is the correct synonym as it also means to make something stronger or more durable. (मजबूत करना)
 
 
• **Example:** Regular exercise helps to strengthen your muscles and improve overall health.
 
 
• Hence, we can conclude that the correct synonym for 'Fortify' is **'Strengthen'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. Strengthen**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Weaken** (कमजोर करना): To reduce the strength, power, or intensity of something.
 
 
• **Example:** The storm weakened after reaching the land.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Broke** (तोड़ देना): To cause something to split, shatter, or separate into pieces.
 
 
• **Example:** She accidentally broke the vase while cleaning the table.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Remove** (हटाना): To take something away or eliminate it.
 
 
• **Example:** Please remove your shoes before entering the house.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The student responded to the question so logically (1)/ that the audience (2)/ praise his analytical approach repeatedly (3)/ despite the time constraints. (4)

options.text: The student responded to the question so logically (1)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is located in part (3) of the sentence and involves **tense inconsistency**.
 
• The sentence begins with the verb "**responded**," which is in the simple past tense.
 
• To maintain consistency throughout the sentence, the subsequent action performed by the audience must also be in the past tense.
 
• The present tense verb "**praise**" should be changed to the past tense form "**praised**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The student responded to the question so logically that the audience **praised** his analytical approach repeatedly despite the time constraints."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(1): "The student responded to the question so logically"** – This part is correct; it uses the past tense and the adverb "logically" to modify the action.
 
• **(2): "that the audience"** – This is a correct conjunction ("so... that") used to introduce a result clause.
 
• **(4): "despite the time constraints."** – This is a correct prepositional phrase used to show contrast, and "constraints" is the appropriate plural noun.

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the underlined part of the sentence. If the sentence is already correct, select 'No substitution required'.

The impact of the new regulations on small businesses is likely to be __even more severely than initially anticipated.__

options.text: even more severe as initially anticipated
even more severe than initially anticipated

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**even more severe than initially anticipated**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb **"is"** in the sentence acts as a **linking verb**. Linking verbs require an **adjective** (subject complement) to describe the subject ("the impact"), not an adverb.
 
• Therefore, the adverb **"severely"** must be replaced by the adjective **"severe."**
 
• For the adjective "severe," the comparative form is **"more severe,"** which must be followed by **"than"** to complete the comparison.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The impact of the new regulations on small businesses is likely to be **even more severe than**__ initially anticipated."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "even more severe as"** is incorrect because the comparative "more" requires "than"; "as" is used for comparisons of equality (e.g., "as severe as").
 
• **Option 2: "even severer than"** is technically a comparative form, but **"more severe"** is the standard and preferred choice in formal English.
 
• **Option 4: "No substitution required"** is incorrect because "severely" is an adverb and cannot describe the noun "impact" after a linking verb.

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

They will organize a farewell party for the retiring teacher.

options.text: A farewell party will be organized for the retiring teacher by them.
The retiring teacher was organized a farewell party by them.
They were organizing a farewell party for the retiring teacher.
A farewell party is being organized by them for the retiring teacher.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "They will organize a farewell party for the retiring teacher."
 
• The tense used here is **Future Simple** (will organize).
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "A farewell party" at the beginning as the new subject.
 
• Change the active verb form "will organize" to "will be organized" (Structure: *Subject + will be + Past Participle (V3)*).
 
• Include the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "them."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A farewell party will be organized for the retiring teacher by them."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The retiring teacher was organized..." – Incorrect tense (Simple Past) and misidentifies the logical object.
 
• **Option 3: **"They were organizing..." – Incorrect tense (Past Continuous) and remains in the active voice.
 
• **Option 4: **"A farewell party is being organized..." – Incorrect tense (Present Continuous passive).

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

The artist was painting a mural that depicted the evolution of civilization.

options.text: A mural that depicted the evolution of civilization is painted by the artist.
A mural was painted by the artist that depicted the evolution of civilization.
A mural that depicted the evolution of civilization was being painted by the artist.
The artist had painted a mural that depicted evolution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence, and the tense of the verb must remain consistent.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The artist was painting a mural that depicted the evolution of civilization."
 
• The tense used here is **Past Continuous** (was painting).
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the entire object phrase "A mural that depicted the evolution of civilization" at the beginning as the new subject.
 
• Change the active verb form "was painting" to "was being painted" (Structure for Past Continuous Passive: *Subject + was/were + being + Past Participle*).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the artist."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A mural that depicted the evolution of civilization was being painted by the artist."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"...is painted..." – Incorrect tense (Simple Present passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"...was painted..." – Incorrect tense (Simple Past passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"The artist had painted..." – Incorrect tense (Past Perfect) and remains in the active voice.

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a correct sentence:

P: because of heavy rains

Q: many trains

R: in northern India

S: were delayed
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (2)** i.e. **QRPS**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sequence begins with "many trains" (Q), which introduces the subject of the sentence.
 
• It is followed by "were delayed" (R), explaining the condition of the trains.
 
• Next, "in northern India" (P) specifies the location of the delay.
 
• Finally, "because of heavy rains" (S) provides the reason for the delays, completing the logical flow of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **QRPS.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (QPRS):** This option places "because of heavy rains" before "in northern India," which disrupts the logical flow of information and makes the sentence less cohesive.
 
• **Option 3 (PRSQ):** Starting with "in northern India" creates ambiguity as the subject of the sentence ("many trains") is introduced later, making the sequence grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4 (PQRS):** This option places "in northern India" before the subject of the sentence ("many trains"), which breaks the logical structure and fails to convey the intended meaning clearly.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The instructions were being read by the students when the bell rang.

options.text: The students were reading the instructions when the bell rang.
The students had read the instructions when the bell rang.
The instructions had been read by the students.
The students have read the instructions when the bell rang.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The agent performing the action (the students) in the passive voice becomes the subject of the active voice sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The instructions were being read by the students when the bell rang."
 
• The tense used here is **Past Continuous** (were being read).
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the agent "The students" at the beginning as the new subject.
 
• Change the passive verb form "were being read" to "were reading" (Past continuous active structure: *was/were + verb-ing*).
 
• Place the object "the instructions" after the verb and retain the subordinate clause "when the bell rang."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The students were reading the instructions when the bell rang."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The students had read..." – Incorrect tense (Past Perfect).
 
• **Option 3: **"The instructions had been read..." – Remains in the passive voice and uses the incorrect tense (Past Perfect).
 
• **Option 4: **"The students have read..." – Incorrect tense (Present Perfect).

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The files have been submitted by the interns before the deadline.

options.text: The interns have submitted the files before the deadline.
The interns submitted the files before the deadline.
The files were submitted before the deadline.
The interns are submitting the files before the deadline.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The agent (the interns) who was performing the action in the passive sentence becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The files have been submitted by the interns before the deadline."
 
• The tense used here is **Present Perfect** (have been submitted).
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the agent "The interns" at the beginning as the new subject.
 
• Change the passive verb form "have been submitted" to the active form "have submitted" (Structure: *Subject + has/have + V3 + Object*).
 
• Place the object "the files" after the verb, followed by the time phrase "before the deadline."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The interns have submitted the files before the deadline."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The interns submitted..." – Incorrect tense (Simple Past).
 
• **Option 3: **"The files were submitted..." – Remains in the passive voice and changes the tense to Simple Past.
 
• **Option 4: **"The interns are submitting..." – Incorrect tense (Present Continuous).

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

Ram said to his sister, "Have you completed your assignment?"

options.text: Ram asked his sister whether she had completed her assignment.
Ram asked his sister has she completed her assignment.
Ram asked his sister if she has completed her work.
Ram said to his sister if she completed the work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Ram asked his sister whether she had completed her assignment.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• In interrogative sentences, the reporting verb **"said to"** is changed to **"asked"**, "enquired", or "wondered". Here, "asked" is used.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• For "Yes/No" questions (starting with an auxiliary verb like 'Have'), we use **"if"** or **"whether"** as a connector between the reporting verb and the reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change:**
 
 
• The direct speech is in the **Present Perfect tense** ("Have... completed").
 
• In indirect speech, it changes to the **Past Perfect tense** (**"had completed"**).
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The second-person pronoun **"you"** changes to **"she"** to match the object of the reporting verb ("his sister").
 
• The possessive adjective **"your"** changes to **"her"**.
 
 
 
• **Sentence Structure:**
 
 
• The interrogative structure ("Have you...") is changed to an **assertive structure** ("she had..."). The question mark is replaced by a full stop.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Ram asked his sister whether she had completed her assignment."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Ram asked his sister has she completed her assignment." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change the tense to past (**"has"** instead of **"had"**) and retains the interrogative word order.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Ram asked his sister if she has completed her work." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change the tense to past (**"has"**) and changes the specific noun **"assignment"** to **"work"**.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Ram said to his sister if she completed the work." 
 
 
• Incorrect reporting verb (**"said to"** should be **"asked"**) and incorrect tense (Simple Past **"completed"** instead of Past Perfect).

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

The manager said, "When will the report be ready?"

options.text: The manager asked when the report would be ready.
The manager told when report will be ready.
The manager asked if report was ready.
The manager questioned that when the report will be ready.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The manager asked when the report would be ready.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• In interrogative sentences, the reporting verb **"said"** is changed to **"asked"**, "enquired", or "wondered".
 
 
 
• **Connector (Wh- word):**
 
 
• When a direct question begins with a question word (who, which, what, where, **when**, etc.), no conjunction (like 'if' or 'that') is used. The question word itself acts as the connector.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change:**
 
 
• The modal **"will"** in direct speech is changed to its past form **"would"** in indirect speech because the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Sentence Structure:**
 
 
• The interrogative form ("will the report be") is converted into the **assertive form** ("the report would be"). The question mark is replaced by a full stop.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The manager asked when the report would be ready."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses **"told"** (which is not used for questions) and fails to change **"will"** to **"would."**
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it uses **"if,"** which is only used for Yes/No questions, and it changes the meaning/tense significantly ("was ready").
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because **"that"** cannot be used as a conjunction before a Wh- question word in indirect speech, and it fails to change **"will"** to **"would."**

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

She said that she would call me later.

options.text: She said, "I will call you later."
She said, "I shall call you late."
She said, "I must call you late."
She said, "She would call me later."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she would call me later.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The third-person pronoun **"she"** (the subject of the reported speech) refers to the speaker. In direct speech, it changes back to the first-person pronoun **"I"**.
 
• The first-person pronoun **"me"** (the object) refers to the person being spoken to. In direct speech, it changes back to **"you"**.
 
 
 
• **Modal/Tense Change:**
 
 
• The modal **"would"** in indirect speech is the past form of **"will"**. To revert to direct speech, "would" changes back to **"will"**.
 
 
 
• **Removal of Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"**, which connects the reporting verb and the reported speech in indirect form, is removed and replaced by a comma and quotation marks.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The spoken words are enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• The first letter of the direct speech (**"I"**) is capitalized.
 
• A comma separates the reporting clause from the quoted speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“She said, "I will call you later."”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "She said, 'I shall call you late.'" 

 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the word **"later"** (comparative adverb) to **"late"** (adjective/adverb), which significantly alters the meaning of the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She said, 'I must call you late.'" 
 
 
• Incorrect because it uses the modal **"must"** (obligation) instead of "will" (future intent) and also changes "later" to **"late."**
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said, 'She would call me later.'" 
 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to convert the third-person pronouns (**"She"**) back to first-person (**"I"**) and retains the indirect modal form (**"would"**).

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The teacher advised the student not to waste time.

options.text: The teacher said, "Do not waste time."
The teacher told the student, "You must study."
The teacher said, "You should not waste time."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The teacher advised the student not to waste time.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Sentence Type:**
 
 
• The indirect speech uses the structure **"advised + object + not + to-infinitive,"** which is the standard way to report a **negative imperative** sentence (a command or piece of advice starting with "Do not").
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The verb **"advised"** in indirect speech often stems from **"said"** or **"said to"** in direct speech when the context implies a suggestion or instruction.
 
 
 
• **Verb Transformation:**
 
 
• The phrase **"not to waste"** in indirect speech is converted back to **"Do not waste"** in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• The reporting clause is separated by a comma.
 
• The imperative sentence inside the quotes starts with a capital letter (**"Do"**).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The teacher said, "Do not waste time."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Changes the entire meaning and vocabulary of the sentence from **"waste time"** to **"must study."**
 
• **Option 3:** Contains a grammatical error (**"order"** instead of "ordered") and uses a less common phrasing (**"Waste no time"**) which doesn't align as perfectly with the "not to waste" transformation.
 
• **Option 4:** **"You should not waste time"** is an assertive/modal sentence. If converted to indirect speech, it would typically use the conjunction **"that"** (e.g., "The teacher said **that** he should not waste time").

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a correct sentence:

P: despite being accused

Q: they

R: remained silent

S: of misconduct
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3)** i.e. **PSQR**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the introductory phrase "Despite being accused," which is **part (P).**
 
• In English grammar, the verb "accused" is idiomatically followed by the preposition "of." This creates a logical mandatory pair between **part (P)** and **part (S)** ("of misconduct").
 
• Following the introductory dependent clause (PS), the main clause must start with a subject. **Part (Q)** "they" serves as the subject of the sentence.
 
• **Part (R)** "remained silent" provides the predicate (action) for the subject, completing the thought logically and grammatically.

Therefore, the correct sequence is **PSQR**, forming the sentence: *"Despite being accused of misconduct, they remained silent."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (PQRS):** This sequence places "they remained silent" between "accused" and "of misconduct," which breaks the grammatical link of the phrasal verb "accused of."
 
• **Option 2 (QRPS):** Although "They remained silent despite being accused of misconduct" is a grammatically valid sentence, in standardized tests, the structure beginning with the introductory phrase (PSQR) is typically favored to test clause recognition.
 
• **Option 4 (QSPR):** This arrangement is nonsensical as it places "of misconduct" immediately after the subject "they" without a connecting verb or context.

questions.question:
**Arrange the parts to form a correct sentence:**
(1) Many people began calling the airline's helpline for refund.
(2) The passengers waited anxiously near the boarding gate.
(3) The airline staff finally announced that the flight was cancelled.
(4) The departure time kept getting postponed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes events in a sequence that involve the postponement of a flight and the final cancellation.
 
• **Sentence 4 is the first sentence** as it introduces the problem:
 
 
• "The departure time kept getting postponed."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 2 follows** as it describes the reaction of the passengers:
 
 
• "The passengers waited anxiously near the boarding gate."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3 is the third sentence** because it provides the next major event:
 
 
• "The airline staff finally announced that the flight was cancelled."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1 is the fourth sentence** as it describes the aftermath of the cancellation:
 
 
• "Many people began calling the airline's helpline for refund."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **4 → 2 → 3 → 1**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The departure time kept getting postponed. The passengers waited anxiously near the boarding gate. The airline staff finally announced that the flight was cancelled. Many people began calling the airline's helpline for refund."

• The sequence of sentences needs to be arranged logically to form a coherent paragraph.
 
• **Sentence 2** is the first sentence as it introduces the object, a leather-bound diary that was purchased: 
 
 
• "She bought a diary."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 4** follows as it describes the diary's appearance, connecting to the previous sentence: 
 
 
• "It was leather-bound."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1** comes next as it explains the purpose of the diary: 
 
 
• "She wrote her thoughts daily."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3** is the last sentence, logically concluding the paragraph with where the diary was kept:

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a correct sentence:
(1) The speaker cleared his throat.
(2) He began his address.
(3) The audience listened intently.
(4) The hall fell silent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sequence of events in the question is logical and follows a cause-and-effect pattern.
 
• **Sentence 1** is the first sentence as it introduces the action of the speaker clearing his throat to begin addressing the audience.
 
• **Sentence 4** follows next, as the hall falling silent is a natural reaction to the speaker preparing to speak.
 
• **Sentence 2** comes third, as the speaker begins his address after the hall becomes silent.
 
• **Sentence 3** is the last sentence, as the audience listens intently to the speaker's address.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is **1-4-2-3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When arranging sentences, pay attention to the logical sequence of events and ensure that each sentence flows naturally into the next.
 
• Look for introductory actions, reactions, and concluding statements to determine the proper order.

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:**

"The speaker cleared his throat. The hall fell silent. He began his address. The audience listened intently."</div

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with appropriate parts of speech.

The Mona Lisa is the best ________ of Leonardo da Vinci.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**creation**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires a **noun** to serve as the object following the superlative adjective **"best."**
 
• **"Creation"** is a noun that refers to a thing that has been made or invented, especially a work of art.
 
• In this context, it correctly identifies the *Mona Lisa* as a product of Leonardo da Vinci's work.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The Mona Lisa is the best **creation**__ of Leonardo da Vinci."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "create"** is a **verb**. Verbs indicate actions and cannot follow an adjective like "best" in this structure.
 
• **Option 2: "creative"** is an **adjective**. It describes a noun (e.g., "a creative artist") but cannot be the noun itself in this position.
 
• **Option 4: "creativity"** is a **noun**, but it refers to the *ability* or *quality* of being imaginative, whereas "creation" refers to the result of that process.

questions.question:
Identify the error in the sentence.

She ran into the list to make sure she hadn't missed anything.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition "**into**" as part of the phrasal verb in Option 3.
 
• The phrasal verb "**run into**" means to meet someone by chance or to collide with something (e.g., "I ran into an old friend").
 
• When referring to examining, reviewing, or checking a list or text quickly, the correct phrasal verb is "**run through**" or "**run over**."
 
• Therefore, "into" should be replaced with "**through**" or "**over**" to make the sentence contextually correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She **ran through** the list to make sure she hadn't missed anything."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ran (Option 1):** This is the correct past tense form of "run." The tense is consistent with the second half of the sentence ("hadn't missed").
 
• **Missed (Option 2):** This is the correct past participle used with "hadn't" to form the past perfect tense, which appropriately describes an action completed before another past action.
 
• **List (Option 4):** This is the correct noun being acted upon; there is no grammatical error in using this word here.

questions.question: Choose the correct one word substitution for: "Secret or disguised language, often used by a particular group."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Argot**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Argot"** refers to a secret or specialized language used by a particular group, often to communicate discreetly or exclude outsiders. (गुप्त भाषा)
 
 
• **Example:** The thieves communicated in an argot that only they understood.
 
 
• It is often associated with groups such as criminals, tradespeople, or specific communities who use this language to keep their communications private.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Argot**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Jargon **(पेशेवर शब्दावली): Technical or specialized language used within a particular profession or group.
 
 
• **Example:** Medical professionals often use jargon that can be difficult for patients to understand.
 
 
 
• **Dialect **(बोली): A regional variety of a language distinguished by vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation.
 
 
• **Example:** She speaks a dialect of Spanish that is common in northern Spain.
 
 
 
• **Idiom **(मुहावरा): A phrase or expression whose meaning is different from the literal interpretation of the words.
 
 
• **Example:** “Break the ice” is an idiom that means to initiate conversation in a social setting.
